correctness.rationale: For n>=3 each row has exactly one missing palette colour, hence at most one rich edge in that row. Total rich-neighbor requires two adjacent rich edges; their unique shared column forces complementary row omissions and a derangement on n-1 remaining colours. This is a bijection giving n(n+1)n(n-1)! D_{n-1}. Automorphisms and colour relabellings act by conjugation and inversion of the derangement, giving cycle types with no 1-cycles. The proper-colouring count is (n+1)!(D_{n+1}+D_n), hence the exact fraction and asymptotic. Direct graph-adjacency enumeration for n=2..8 corroborates every formula; the infinite proof is deductive.

value.rationale: The question of how many extremal colourings exist is motivated by the sharp 2026 bipartite index theorem. The all-optima rigidity classification gives the exact named count and a complete structural orbit classification by cycle types over an unbounded natural family. The probability among proper minimum-palette colourings is asymptotically 1/n, quantifying rarity. Neither these counts nor optimizer types follow from the value of the optimum index alone.
